script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 29. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Remember how summer vacation felt endless as a child?  Now years vanish in a blur.  Time hasn't changed—something in you has.

Children experience constant novelty—every day brings new information. Adults live in routine—same commute, same tasks. Your brain doesn't bother encoding routine, so fewer memories form. Fewer memories mean time seems faster in retrospect. During accidents or threats, people report time slowing dramatically.  Research shows the brain processes more information per second during danger.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Want more life?  Seek novelty.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Time Expansion - Introduce Novelty.

Here's your activity: Do one thing today that breaks your routine—take a different route, try a new food, have a conversation with someone new. Pay attention to details. Notice if the day feels slightly longer in retrospect. This helps you slow down subjective time through new experiences.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why time feels different can be applied to time expansion - introduce novelty. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
